lines: Hi. I'm {npc_name}.
I do not think we have properly met, Lamb.
Um. I'm {npc_name}.
Sorry, I am trying to place you, but nothing is landing.
My name is {npc_name}.
Before you ask, I am not sure you should be trusting strangers with this.
Oh. Lamb, right?
I'm {npc_name}. We have crossed paths around {city} enough times that your face stuck.
I'm {npc_name}.
We are not close, but I know your name, and I know people have been worried.
I'm {npc_name}.
I live near your building, so I notice more than I probably should.
Lamb... I'm {npc_name}.
We are neighbors. Not friends exactly, but close enough that your door being quiet felt wrong.
It's me, {npc_name}.
We were at school together, back when {city} still felt too big for everyone.
I'm {npc_name}.
We knew each other at school, though I do not know what that makes me to you now.
Hey, Lamb. I'm {npc_name}.
We overlapped at {university}; same late rooms, same tired faces.
I'm {npc_name}.
You probably do not remember me, but I remember enough campus nonsense for both of us.
I'm {npc_name}.
We worked around each other enough that I learned your habits before I learned how to pronounce half our clients' names.
I'm {npc_name}.
I know you mostly through other people's stories, so I should be honest about that first.
I'm {npc_name}.
I will tell you what I can, but please hold it gently.
Before I say anything else, I should warn you.
This is not something I can swear to. The source is {source}.
It might help, or it might just give you another wrong shape to carry.
Do you still want to hear it?
accept_prefix_lines: Then I will give it to you carefully.
decline_lines: That may be kinder than collecting every loose story people throw at you.

lines: I do have something, but it is messy.
It came through {source}, so please do not carve it into stone.
Do you want the messy version anyway?
decline_lines: Probably the healthiest thing anyone has said in this town today.

lines: I can answer, but not cleanly.
What I know is tangled up with {source}.
If I tell you, you have to decide whether it belongs in that book.
Do you want it?
accept_prefix_lines: Do not mistake this for certainty.
decline_lines: Some things are worse when they pretend to be answers.

memory_bridge_lines: If you want the rest of what I remember...
This might connect to something else.
I should probably mention one more piece.

lines: Sorry... I do not think we have met.
You look shaken, and I wish I had something steadier to give you.
But I would rather tell you nothing than hand you a wrong memory.
Do I know you?
...No. I do not think I do.
That probably makes me the wrong person to ask.
You are asking strangers to tell you who you are?
That sounds dangerous.
Please be careful with whatever people say.
No. I do not know you.
I am sorry, but I have nothing useful.
Ask someone who can look you in the eye and mean it.
I have seen you around, Lamb.
That is the honest version.
I do not know you well enough to give you a memory I would trust.
I could make something up, but that feels like a terrible hobby.
All I know is your name and the way people lower their voices when they say it lately.
That is not a memory. It is just noise.
Your birthday came up at the cafe once.
Someone teased you about being twenty-five and still ordering drinks like a student.
You laughed, so I remember it.
I thought you were younger.
Twenty-two, maybe?
Do not hold that too tightly. I might be borrowing someone else's certainty.
You usually come home alone.
One set of lights, one set of footsteps, one window left open too late.
If someone lives with you, they are very good at being invisible.
I always assumed Saeli lived with you.
She is there enough on weekends that people started treating it like fact.
Assumptions grow legs around here.
There was another pair of shoes outside your door for a while.
I thought maybe you had a roommate.
But shoes are not exactly a witness statement.
Naven's name still comes up when people talk about you.
For a long time I thought you still lived with him.
Old information has a way of pretending it is current.
You used to get letters from home.
Not Merun City home. Family home.
You said they were far enough away that visits had to be planned like weather.
Oryn is your little brother, right?
You complained about him like it was a sport.
But you kept every tiny drawing he sent you.
I heard Oryn was your older brother.
Or maybe he just acted older in the story.
People tidy family stories until they stop being true.
Someone told me Oryn was your cousin.
They said it with that awful confidence people use when they do not know a family.
So... take that carefully.
You arrived in Merun City before Sorel was even part of the conversation.
High school first. New uniform, too-clean bag, pretending you were not nervous.
Everyone pretended not to notice. Everyone noticed.
I thought you came to Merun for university.
That is how most of us met you, so it became the easy version.
Easy versions are not always true.
I heard you only moved here after university for work.
It made sense when someone said it.
A lot of wrong things make sense until someone remembers better.
Naven used to wait near the school gate when the rain got bad.
You acted embarrassed, but you always walked home with him.
I remember thinking you were lucky and trying not to envy it.
People said you lived in a student dorm back then.
I never saw it myself.
It might have just been the kind of thing classmates say when they do not know where someone goes after class.
You always seemed so independent that I assumed you already had your own place.
Even in high school.
Looking back, that might say more about how you carried yourself than where you slept.
You were the person teachers looked at when no one else knew the answer.
It was irritating.
Useful, but irritating.
Design was always your thing.
At Sorel, you could make a blank room look like it was waiting for someone specific.
That sounds sentimental, but it was annoying how good you were.
People kept calling you an architecture student.
You had the rulers, the models, the exhausted stare.
Maybe they rounded you into the nearest word.
I heard engineering once.
Maybe because you spent time in that building when the design rooms were full.
Campus rumors have terrible maps.
You got your own place when university started.
Tiny, from what you said, but yours.
You talked about choosing curtains like it was a declaration of independence.
I thought you stayed with Naven through university.
People kept linking you two in stories.
Maybe they forgot that lives keep moving after the first chapter.
I placed you in the dorms in my head.
Most of us were there, and you were always around late.
That does not mean you slept there.
Interior designer. That is the part I know.
You once rearranged a waiting room while you were only there to drop off papers.
The owner kept it that way.
I called you an architect once.
You gave me a look like I had moved a wall without asking.
So maybe that was my mistake, not your job.
Someone said graphic designer because they saw your sketches.
Your work did have pages and color notes everywhere.
But sketches can point to a lot of things.
I used to think you worked at the flower shop.
You were in there so often that it seemed reasonable.
Reasonable is not the same as true.
You finished Sorel and went straight into work.
You tried to act casual about it.
But you kept checking your first client email like it might disappear.
Roses, usually red ones.
You pretended you were choosing them for the room, but you smiled before you paid.
People do not smile at design research like that.
Lilies stick in my head when I think of you.
Maybe you bought them once.
Maybe I just remember the smell and attached your face to it.
Sunflowers felt like your sort of flower.
Bright, impossible to ignore, always taking up too much space on the counter.
That is not evidence. It is just a feeling.
Red kept showing up around you.
Notebook corners, fabric samples, that awful scarf you insisted was tasteful.
You liked it too much for it to be an accident.
Blue was always in your layouts, so I assumed it was your favorite.
You used it carefully, like you trusted it.
But trusting a color for work is not the same as loving it.
You always asked for extra spice.
Then acted calm while your eyes watered.
It was either bravery or poor survival instinct.
I saw you push away a spicy dish once.
After that I thought you hated the stuff.
One bad lunch can become a whole personality if people are lazy.
You asked whether something was mild.
I remember that part.
I do not remember whether you were asking for yourself or for Saeli.
Dessert never seemed to move you much.
Everyone else fought over the last sweet roll.
You looked like you were waiting for the argument to end.
I heard you had a huge sweet tooth.
Maybe because you kept bringing pastries to people.
Buying them and wanting them are two different things, though.
You once said, 'I hate desserts,' but I think you were trapped at a terrible party.
That sentence might have been about the room, not the cake.
Still, it stuck.
Science-fiction was the only movie shelf you defended like a legal case.
You said good rooms and good spaceships had the same problem.
They both had to make impossible places feel lived in.
Someone told me romance movies were your favorite.
Then someone else laughed like that was the worst possible answer.
So I am not sure which person I should believe either.
You picked horror once and everyone made it your whole taste.
That happens when a quiet person chooses something loud.
Maybe it was a favorite. Maybe it was just the only thing no one had seen.
Romance movies made you impatient.
You always complained that nobody in them knew how to talk like an adult.
Saeli said that was rich coming from you.
You once brought soup that tasted like boiled regret.
You apologized before anyone opened the lid.
That was probably the safest part of the meal.
I heard you were an excellent cook.
But now that I say it, I think Saeli was laughing when she told the story.
That changes the shape of it.
You walk everywhere.
Rain, heat, late evenings, it does not matter.
If that counts as exercise, then yes, you exercise constantly.
I saw you carrying a gym bag a few times.
Or what looked like one.
With you it might have been fabric samples and three kinds of tape.
You were always half-running down the street.
I thought maybe you ran for exercise.
Now I wonder if you were just late a lot.
Sports made you vanish.
If someone suggested a game, you suddenly remembered urgent work in another building.
It was almost graceful.
I remember you at a school sports day.
You were smiling, so I assumed you liked playing.
You might have been laughing at someone else falling over.
I saw you near the match crowds sometimes.
That made people call you a sports fan.
But Merun streets get crowded whether you care about the score or not.
Hot weather made you personally offended.
You once blamed the sun for a bad floor plan.
Nobody argued because you looked ready to fight the window.
I thought you liked hot summer days.
You were always outside when everyone else hid indoors.
Maybe you were not enjoying it. Maybe you just had places to be.
You stopped for cats and dogs like they were neighbors with voting rights.
Even the mean little ones got a greeting.
That is hard to fake.
I thought you liked dogs more than cats.
There was one cat you avoided for weeks.
To be fair, that cat avoided being kind.
You once said you did not want animals around.
But I think there was mud on your shoes and a dog involved.
People say dramatic things when their socks are wet.
You were not loud, but you were never alone for long.
People drifted toward you after class.
Saeli was usually first, but not the only one.
I thought you kept to yourself.
You always looked busy, head down, pencil moving.
Maybe I mistook focus for loneliness.
From the outside, it looked like you never had a real group.
Just people passing through.
But outside views miss the doorways people actually use.
Saeli was the first name people paired with yours.
Not because you were the same person.
Because wherever one of you was, the other was usually close enough to interrupt.
People exaggerate how close you and Saeli were.
That is what I heard, anyway.
Maybe being seen together made everyone invent the feeling.
Near the end, people said you and Saeli could not stand each other.
I saw the quiet between you once and believed it.
But quiet can mean anger, hurt, or just not knowing what to say.
Saeli is not just someone from before.
She still comes by, still waits for you, still looks worried when your door stays dark.
That looks like love from where I stand.
I heard you and Saeli were only friends.
Maybe someone said it before they knew better.
Or maybe people say 'only' when a thing scares them.
There was a rumor Saeli was your ex.
I think it started after someone saw you two arguing outside the flower shop.
Arguments are easy to mistake for endings.
You and Saeli changed during university.
Not suddenly, no matter what people say.
It was more like everyone else noticed at the same time.
Saeli is still at Sorel.
She complains about deadlines with the special despair of someone who has not escaped yet.
You used to bring her coffee when she forgot meals existed.
I thought Saeli had already graduated.
She carries herself like someone done with being graded.
That might be confidence, not a diploma.
Weekends are when Saeli usually shows up.
Same bag, same tired knock, same way of checking the street before you open the door.
It happened often enough to become part of the rhythm here.
I heard Saeli only came around on holidays.
Maybe whoever said that only noticed the big visits.
Some people miss the ordinary days and then call their version complete.

opening_lines: Funny. I spent all this time trying to find the place I belong, and I am still not completely sure I found the person who belongs there.
I could not have gotten here without you.
So before I go, tell me something.
Do you think we got it right?
The memories. Me. Do you think we actually figured out who I am?

confidence_choices.text: I think so... but I'm not completely sure.
No. I think we got some of it wrong.

HIGH_CONFIDENT: Some of it still feels strange, like reading someone else's diary and recognizing the handwriting.
But when I put everything together, it feels like me.
HIGH_UNSURE: I am the one missing half my life, and somehow I sound more confident than you.
We made mistakes. I know there are things we will never hold perfectly.
I think we did better than you think.
HIGH_DOUBTFUL: Maybe we did get pieces wrong.
But I do not feel lost the way I did before.
Maybe knowing yourself is not about remembering every detail perfectly.
And I think you got pretty close.
MIXED_CONFIDENT: I wish I could borrow that certainty.
Some things fit. Some really do not.
There are memories in that book that feel like they belong to three different lives.
Maybe one of them is me.
Maybe all of them are, in some way.
I am just not as certain as you are.
MIXED_UNSURE: That is exactly how I feel.
There are pieces that fit perfectly, and others that feel like we forced them into the wrong places.
Maybe that is all we were ever going to get.
Not an answer. Just enough pieces to keep going.
MIXED_DOUBTFUL: But I do not think everything was wrong.
There are things in there I want to keep.
People I want to meet again. Places I want to see.
Maybe that is enough for now.
LOW_CONFIDENT: I keep looking at everything we decided, and none of it feels like it is looking back at me.
Maybe this really is who I was.
Because I do not recognize her.
LOW_UNSURE: Actually, I think I am less sure now than when we started.
Before, I knew I did not remember.
Now I have answers, and I do not know which ones belong to me.
I wanted this to make things clearer.
LOW_DOUBTFUL: I wanted to believe we would reach the end and everything would suddenly make sense.
I guess that is not how this works.
Maybe we got lost somewhere along the way.
At least you are not pretending we did not.

thank_you_lines: For listening to all of them.
For trying to figure me out when I could not.
Maybe we found the old me.
But I do not think I am as lost as I was when we started.

MIXED: Whatever is on the other side, I will find out.
LOW: I think I can do this part myself.
